title: Rigveda 9.1: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.1: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.1 is a hymn of 10 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 667r-667v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.1.1-2 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 7, varga 16); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 667r
translation.original_text:
1svādi̍ṣṭhayā̱ madi̍ṣṭhayā̱ pava̍sva soma̱ dhāra̍yā | indrā̍ya̱ pāta̍ve su̱taḥ ||
2ra̱kṣo̱hā vi̱śvaca̍rṣaṇir a̱bhi yoni̱m ayo̍hatam | druṇā̍ sa̱dhastha̱m āsa̍dat ||
translation.text:
1In sweetest and most gladdening stream flow pure, O Soma, on thy way, Pressed out for Indra, for his drink.
2Fiend-queller, Friend of all men, he hath with the wood attained unto His place, his iron-fashioned home.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 667r (numbered 89r by the scribe) (OPenn image 667, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 8.103.10 ‹āsāva atithim agnim rathānām›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 667v (numbered 89v by the scribe), begins in RV 9.1.3 ‹-vṛtrahan-tamaḥ parṣi rādhaḥ maghonām›. Verses 9.1.1-2 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1svādiṣṭhayā | madiṣṭhayā | pavasva | soma | dhārayā | indrāya | pātave | sutaḥ
2rakṣaḥ-hā | viśva-carṣaṇiḥ | abhi | yonim | ayaḥ-hatam | druṇā | sadha-stham | ā | asadat

translation.original_ref: RV 9.1.3-10 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 7, varga 16); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 667v
translation.original_text:
3va̱ri̱vo̱dhāta̍mo bhava̱ maṁhi̍ṣṭho vṛtra̱hanta̍maḥ | parṣi̱ rādho̍ ma̱ghonā̍m ||
4a̱bhy a̍rṣa ma̱hānā̍ṁ de̱vānā̍ṁ vī̱tim andha̍sā | a̱bhi vāja̍m u̱ta śrava̍ḥ ||
5tvām acchā̍ carāmasi̱ tad id artha̍ṁ di̱ve-di̍ve | indo̱ tve na̍ ā̱śasa̍ḥ ||
6pu̱nāti̍ te pari̱sruta̱ṁ soma̱ṁ sūrya̍sya duhi̱tā | vāre̍ṇa̱ śaśva̍tā̱ tanā̍ ||
7tam ī̱m aṇvī̍ḥ sama̱rya ā gṛ̱bhṇanti̱ yoṣa̍ṇo̱ daśa̍ | svasā̍ra̱ḥ pārye̍ di̱vi ||
8tam ī̍ṁ hinvanty a̱gruvo̱ dhama̍nti bāku̱raṁ dṛti̍m | tri̱dhātu̍ vāra̱ṇam madhu̍ ||
9a̱bhī̱3̱̍mam aghnyā̍ u̱ta śrī̱ṇanti̍ dhe̱nava̱ḥ śiśu̍m | soma̱m indrā̍ya̱ pāta̍ve ||
10a̱syed indro̱ made̱ṣv ā viśvā̍ vṛ̱trāṇi̍ jighnate | śūro̍ ma̱ghā ca̍ maṁhate ||
translation.text:
3Be thou best Vr̥itra-slayer, best granter of bliss, most liberal: Promote our wealthy princes' gifts.
4Flow onward with thy juice unto the banquet of the Mighty Gods: Flow bither for our strength and fame.
5O Indu, we draw nigh to thee, with this one object day by day: To thee alone our prayers are said
6By means of this eternal fleece may Sûrya's Daughter purify Thy Soma that is foaming forth.
7Ten sister maids of slender form seize him within the press and hold Him firmly on the final day.
8The virgins send him forth: they blow the the skin musician-like and fuse The triple foe-repelling meath.
9Inviolable milch-kine round about him blend for Indra's drink, The fresh young Soma with their milk.
10In the wild raptures of this draught, Indra slays all the Vr̥itras: he, The Hero, pours his wealth on us.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 667v (numbered 89v by the scribe) (OPenn image 668, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.1.3 ‹-vṛtrahan-tamaḥ parṣi rādhaḥ maghonām›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 668r (numbered 90r by the scribe), begins in RV 9.2.3 ‹-dhārā sutasya vedhasaḥ apaḥ›. Verses 9.1.3-10 end on this page; 9.1.3 begins on fol. 667r (numbered 89r by the scribe).
